digest.top_line: FIRESTORM: dose-escalated postop RT (BED ≥79.2 Gy) for high-risk meningioma, 5-yr PFS 65.8% vs 38.8%, MVA HR 0.40, no excess G3+ necrosis.
digest.tldr: CNS carried the day, both readings on the same question: how much RT a meningioma needs. FIRESTORM says escalate past 66 Gy/33 fx in grade 2-3 disease (HR 0.40, PFS only, OS HR 0.66 P=.27); RTOG 0539's 12-yr f/u anchors the standard-dose benchmark at 72.2% 10-yr PFS after 54 Gy. Breast adds RAPCHEM: 2.4% 10-yr LRR omitting nodal RT after NAC response, awaiting B-51.

sites.intro: Response-adapted nodal RT omission after NAC, single-arm and ALND-era, so the randomised answer is still B-51's.

studies.name: RAPCHEM
studies.tldr: 10yr locoregional recurrence 2.9% (24/838) with response-adapted post-NAC RT, including 2.4% in low-risk pts given breast-only or no RT.
details: 🔍 Prospective multicenter cohort (BOOG 2010-03), N=848, 17 Dutch centers, accrual 2011-2015, 10yr f/u
🔍 Eligibility: cT1-2 (<5cm) cN1 (1-3 involved nodes), all received neoadjuvant chemo then surgery
🔍 RT assigned by ypN status, not randomized: risk group determined by nodal response to NAC
📊 10yr locoregional recurrence by risk group (ypN-based RT allocation)
📐 No dose or fractionation reported in source text; RT field, not dose, was the de-escalation variable
⚠️ Single-arm, no untreated comparator: the paper states it did not compare pts treated with and without RT
⚠️ Most pts had ALND, less common now; SLN-staged pts in current practice are a different population
⚠️ Nodal recurrences pooled into a composite LRR endpoint; isolated regional failure by group not reported in source
🔗 Randomized answer pending from NSABP B-51 (NCT01872975), cited in source as ~3 years out
🗞️ EBCC15 presentation (Abstract 1), Mauritz et al, Maastro; no peer-reviewed manuscript cited in source

verdict.rationale: Single-arm risk-adapted cohort with no untreated comparator; cannot attribute the low LRR to the de-escalated fields rather than to favorable ypN0 biology.
verdict.audience: cT1-2 cN1 breast cancer, post-neoadjuvant chemo + surgery, mostly ALND

studies.significance: The de-escalation variable is target volume, not dose: ypN0 pts got breast-only RT after BCS and none after mastectomy, and still ran 2.4% LRR at 10yr. That is the omission decision this informs, but the cohort is ALND-staged, so it does not transfer cleanly to today's SLN-only pts.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT1-2 cN1 pts converting to ypN0 after neoadjuvant chemo with ALND staging, this supports omitting regional nodal RT (and RT entirely after mastectomy) as low-recurrence-risk evidence; it does not address SLN-only staging or the randomized omission question B-51 is powered for.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective multicenter cohort (**RAPCHEM / BOOG 2010-03**), **N=848** at 17 Dutch centers, 2011-2015, with **10-year** follow-up. Not randomized: RT extent was assigned by post-chemotherapy nodal status.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **cT1-2 (<5 cm), cN1** with 1 to 3 involved nodes at baseline, all treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy then surgery. **Most underwent ALND**, which the authors flag as less common in current practice.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Allocation by **ypN**: ypN0 → breast RT after BCS, **no RT after mastectomy**; ypN1 → breast/chest wall **without regional nodal irradiation**; ypN2+ → breast/chest wall **plus regional nodes**. Dose and fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **24/838 (2.9%)** locoregional recurrences at 10 years without distant disease, and the rate did **not track risk group** (2.4% low, 3.2% intermediate, 2.8% high).

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cT1-2 cN1 breast cancer with ALND after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery. Does not represent SLN-only staged pts, cN2-3 disease, or tumors ≥5 cm.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The flat LRR across all three groups is consistent with successful risk-adaptation but equally with the fields being irrelevant at this event rate, and a **2.9%** ceiling leaves almost no power to separate them. Recurrence site and per-group isolated regional failure are not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The invited discussant framed nodal RT as omittable in low-risk post-mastectomy pts and still advisable in intermediate risk. The authors defer the causal question to **NSABP B-51 (NCT01872975)**, expected in about 3 years.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Target volume, not dose, is what was de-escalated: ypN0 pts received breast-only RT after BCS and none after mastectomy, with 2.4% LRR at 10yr. The flat rate across groups (2.4% / 3.2% / 2.8%) means the tiers cannot be separated at this event rate, and ALND staging gates transfer to SLN-only pts.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Nodal response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy is being used as the allocation variable for local therapy: converting cN1 to ypN0 is what buys the smaller RT field. That raises the stakes on regimen choice and pCR-directed sequencing, though the cohort predates routine SLN-only restaging.

open_questions: Does risk-adapted RT hold with SLN-only staging instead of ALND
Isolated regional vs in-breast failure sites by risk group
Randomized confirmation of nodal RT omission in ypN0

sites.intro: Two meningioma datasets bracket the dose question from opposite ends, neither randomised; NRG BN003 and ROAM remain the tests.

studies.name: RTOG 0539
studies.tldr: 10-yr PFS 85.2% observed low-risk, 72.2% intermediate-risk after 54Gy, 42.5% high-risk after 60Gy; median f/u 12 yrs.
details: 🔍 Phase 2, non-randomised, risk-adapted: 3 prespecified cohorts, N=165 eligible of 244 consented, central path review

details.text: 📐 RT dose by risk: 54Gy/30fx (intermediate), 60Gy/30fx (high); group 1 observed, no RT

details: 📊 Median PFS not reached low- or intermediate-risk; high-risk median PFS 3.8 yrs (95% CI 2.8-11.2)
📊 High-risk median OS 11.2 yrs (95% CI 4.6-not reached)

details.text: 📊 Low-risk grade 1 by extent of resection (10-yr, observation only)
📊 Intermediate-risk cohort: recurrent grade 1 vs newly-dx grade 2 after GTR

details: 📐 High-risk Cox: recurrent disease HR 2.5 (1.01-6.18), p=0.047 for PFS; STR HR 2.58 (1.09-6.11), p=0.031

subdetails: New since prior reports: 2 grade 3 (auditory, neurologic) + 1 grade 4 hemorrhage in intermediate group
Zubrod, MMSE, neurologic function score stable over time (Suppl Tables 4-6)

details: ⚠️ No randomised comparator: adjuvant RT vs observation for GTR grade 2 remains untested here; NRG BN003 and ROAM/EORTC 1308 are the randomised tests
⚠️ Cohorts allocated by risk, not randomised, so cross-cohort comparisons are confounded by grade, resection, and recurrence status
⚠️ 25.0% of intermediate and 22.6% of high-risk pts entered as recurrent by imaging only, no re-resection pathology

verdict.rationale: Non-randomised phase 2, cohorts allocated by risk with no observation control for grade 2 post-GTR. Long f/u makes it the benchmark, not the randomised answer.
verdict.audience: WHO grade 1-3 meningioma, post-GTR/STR or recurrent, Zubrod 0-1

studies.significance: The 10-yr numbers now gate two RT decisions. Low-risk grade 1 post-STR fell to 72.7% PFS vs 88.0% after GTR, supporting RT consideration after STR. And recurrent grade 1 salvaged with 54Gy reached only 67.0% 10-yr OS, worse than newly-dx grade 2 post-GTR (91.0%, HR 0.30, p=0.045), which argues against banking on salvage.
studies.monday_clinic: In newly-diagnosed WHO grade 2 meningioma after GTR, this supports adjuvant 54Gy with 10-yr PFS 72.2% and OS 84.7% pending NRG BN003 and ROAM; it does not settle whether observation would do as well, and offers little for recurrent grade 2-3 disease where 10-yr PFS stayed at 15.0%.

primary_endpoint.name: Progression-free survival (3-yr, previously reported; long-term update)

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multi-arm prospective **phase 2**, non-randomised, risk-adapted allocation to 3 cohorts (NRG/RTOG 0539). Primary endpoint was **3-yr PFS**, reported previously; protocol follow-up continued up to 10 additional years, data cutoff 8/15/2023. Median follow-up **12.1, 12.0, and 11.1 years** for low-, intermediate-, and high-risk.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Adults ≥18, Zubrod **0-1**, histologically confirmed unifocal WHO grade 1-3 meningioma, newly diagnosed or recurrent, any extent of resection. 244 consented, **165 eligible** (60 / 52 / 53). Grouping used centrally confirmed grade, GTR vs STR, and recurrence status.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Group 1 (grade 1 post-GTR/STR) **observed, no RT**. Group 2 (recurrent grade 1 or new grade 2 post-GTR) received **54 Gy in 30 fx**. Group 3 (new grade 2 post-STR, new grade 3, or recurrent grade 2-3) received **60 Gy in 30 fx**.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: 10-yr cumulative incidence of progression **8.9%, 21.2%, 39.3%** across cohorts. Recurrent disease and STR were each independently associated with worse PFS and OS in the high-risk Cox model.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: RT-attributed **grade 3+ AEs in 9.6%** (54 Gy) and **15.1%** (60 Gy). New events since the landmark reports were 2 grade 3 (auditory, neurologic) plus 1 grade 4 hemorrhage in the intermediate group and one high-risk patient with multiple grade 3 events. Zubrod, MMSE, and neurologic function score stayed stable.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents resected or recurrent WHO grade 1-3 meningioma, Zubrod 0-1, treated with conventionally fractionated photon-era RT to 54-60 Gy. Does not represent multifocal disease, poor performance status, or molecularly classified meningioma, since grouping used **histopathologic grade only**.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Cohorts were risk-allocated, not randomised, so grade 2 post-GTR outcomes carry no concurrent observation arm. A quarter of intermediate- and high-risk entries were **recurrent by imaging only**, without re-resection pathology, and WHO grading has since moved toward molecular criteria that would reclassify some of these tumors.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The authors position this as a benchmark: observation for grade 1 post-GTR, RT for intermediate and high risk, with the de-escalation question in grade 2 post-GTR handed to **NRG BN003 (NCT03180268)** and ROAM/EORTC 1308. High-risk outcomes stay poor at 60 Gy, and no effective systemic option exists, so improvement has to come from first-line treatment.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Two decisions move. Post-STR grade 1 fell to 72.7% 10-yr PFS vs 88.0% post-GTR, supporting RT consideration after STR. Salvage after grade 1 recurrence reached only 67.0% 10-yr OS vs 91.0% for upfront-treated grade 2, and 60 Gy left high-risk PFS at 42.5%.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Extent of resection carried independent weight, not just risk-group assignment: in the high-risk Cox model STR vs GTR gave HR 2.58 (1.09-6.11) for PFS and HR 3.38 (1.28-8.91) for OS. Achieving GTR changes which RT pathway a patient enters and its expected 10-yr outcome.

Does molecular classification outperform WHO grade for risk assignment?

studies.name: FIRESTORM
studies.tldr: 5-yr PFS 65.8% vs 38.8% with BED ≥79.2 Gy postop RT for high-risk meningioma; MVA HR 0.40, no excess G3+ necrosis.
details: 📊 1° outcome PFS: 3-yr 86.4% vs 55.6%, 5-yr 65.8% vs 38.8% (P=.0022) DE-RT vs SD-RT
📐 Grade-stratified Cox (PH assumption violated by grade, P=.04): HR 0.40 (0.22-0.73), P=.008
🔍 IPD meta-analysis, 7 institutions, N=248; 75.8% WHO grade 2, 41.5% recurrent, 75.2% STR/biopsy, median f/u 67.1 mo
🔍 DE-RT = BED ≥79.2 Gy (66 Gy/33 fx equivalent) or carbon boost; median BED 82.9 vs 70.1 Gy

subdetails: 68 Gy/31 fx (50 Gy/25 photons + 18 Gy/6 carbon boost): 33 cases, 55.9%
Photon boost PTV margin 0.5-2 mm; carbon boost CTV up to 6 mm

details.text: 📊 PFS benefit persists across sensitivity subgroups (DE-RT vs SD-RT)
⚠️ Radionecrosis: any grade higher with DE-RT, severe events similar
⚠️ Any-grade RN excess is carbon-driven: 15/33 (45%) mixed carbon-photon vs 5/26 (19.2%) photon-alone DE-RT; photon-alone vs SD-RT P=.41

details: ⚠️ All 3 G3+ RN events in DE-RT were in the mixed carbon-photon cohort (3/33, 9.1%); photon-alone 0%
🔗 Photon-alone vs mixed carbon-photon DE-RT: 5-yr PFS 68.3% vs 61.1% (P=.34), so the benefit is not carbon-specific
⚠️ DE-RT delivered at only 2 of 7 institutions (one carbon-only, one photon-only); confounding by center, imaging (DOTATATE PET) and response assessment not capturable by IPTW
⚠️ No molecular data (methylation class, 34-gene score), so the population that actually needs escalation can't be isolated

details.text: ⚠️ SD-RT arm is heterogeneous: 35 cases (18.5%) were focal SRS, mostly 12-18 Gy/1 fx, whose 5-yr PFS was 20.5%, dragging the comparator down

verdict.rationale: Retrospective IPD pooling, non-randomised; DE-RT confined to 2 centers. IPTW plus consistent sensitivity subgroups make the PFS divergence from 60 Gy/30 fx credible but not confirmatory.
verdict.audience: High-risk meningioma per RTOG 0539: STR grade 2, recurrent grade 2, any grade 3

studies.significance: The escalation signal is photon-deliverable: photon-alone DE-RT (70 Gy/35 fx, 66 Gy/33 fx) matched mixed carbon-photon on 5-yr PFS (68.3% vs 61.1%, P=.34) while carrying 0% grade ≥3 RN versus 9.1%. Boost PTV margins were 0.5-2 mm. That moves the dose decision for STR grade 2 and grade 3 disease without needing a carbon facility.
studies.monday_clinic: In postoperative high-risk meningioma per RTOG 0539, particularly Simpson 4-5 residual disease, this supports weighing photon dose escalation above 60 Gy/30 fx over the standard prescription; it does not inform GTR grade 1 disease or claim a survival benefit.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: International **individual patient-level meta-analysis**, 7 institutions, N=248, all retrospective except one prospective trial contributing DE-RT. Median follow-up **67.1 months**. Cox MVA was the prespecified primary analysis, with IPTW as sensitivity.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: High-risk meningioma **per RTOG 0539**: WHO grade 2 after STR/biopsy, any recurrent grade 2, or any grade 3. Median age 60 (range 17-93); **75.8% grade 2**, 41.5% recurrent, 75.2% Simpson 4/STR, 22.2% with prior RT. Biopsy confirmation and at least one post-treatment imaging follow-up required.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **DE-RT defined as BED ≥79.2 Gy** (66 Gy/33 fx equivalent) or any carbon-ion boost; median BED **82.9 vs 70.1 Gy**. Photon DE-RT used sequential or SIB with a boost PTV margin of **0.5-2 mm**, carbon used 16 Gy/8 fx after 50 Gy/25 fx photons with a 6 mm CTV margin. SD-RT used larger CTV margins of 1-2 cm and included 35 SRS cases.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: PFS** from end of RT to in-field recurrence on MRI per RANO-meningioma or death. Secondary: OS and CNS radionecrosis graded by CTCAE v5.0, highest grade at any timepoint.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Whole-cohort 3- and 5-yr PFS were **62.8%** (55.8-69.0%) and **45.0%** (37.3-52.3%); OS 83.4% and 71.6%. The DE-RT split and subgroup sensitivity analyses are in the tables above.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Any-grade RN 18.1% overall, higher with DE-RT (**33.9% vs 13.2%, P=.001**) but grade ≥3 statistically similar (5.1% vs 3.2%, P=.47). The excess concentrated in the mixed carbon-photon cohort (45% any grade, 9.1% grade ≥3) versus **0% grade ≥3 with photon-alone DE-RT**. One grade 5 event in each arm.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Historic 5-yr PFS with 60 Gy/30 fx runs **40% to 60%**, matching the SD-RT arm here. RTOG 0539 used CTV margins of 2 cm to 54 Gy and 1 cm to 60 Gy, far larger than the 0.5-2 mm boost margins used for DE-RT in this cohort.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents postoperative high-risk meningioma per RTOG 0539, predominantly grade 2 after subtotal resection. Does not represent WHO grade 1 disease, GTR grade 2 without other risk features, or molecularly-selected cohorts.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: DE-RT was offered at only **2 of 7 institutions**, one carbon-only and one photon-only, so treatment effect is confounded with center-level practice (DOTATATE PET planning, response assessment, supportive care) that IPTW cannot balance. P values were **not adjusted for multiple testing** across the many subgroup analyses, and the SD-RT comparator mixes conventional fractionation with 35 SRS cases whose 5-yr PFS was 20.5%.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The authors frame this as a benchmark for prospective randomised trials rather than a practice mandate. Molecular classification (methylation class, 34-gene expression score) is the missing axis: proliferative meningiomas derived no benefit from adjuvant RT in prior work, so whether escalation rescues them is untested here.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The escalation signal is photon-deliverable: photon-alone DE-RT (70 Gy/35 fx, 66 Gy/33 fx) matched mixed carbon-photon on 5-yr PFS (68.3% vs 61.1%, P=.34) with 0% grade ≥3 RN versus 9.1%. Boost PTV margins were 0.5-2 mm, so the dose decision moves without a carbon facility.

papers.title: Long-Term Analysis of NRG Oncology RTOG 0539: A Phase II Trial of Observation for Low-Risk Meningioma and Radiotherapy for Intermediate- and High-Risk Meningioma
papers.abstract: NRG Oncology RTOG 0539 was a prospective phase II trial of risk-adapted radiotherapy for patients with WHO grade 1-3 meningioma. Low-risk (group 1, n = 60) was defined as a grade 1 tumor after gross total resection or subtotal resection (GTR/STR) and prospectively monitored. Intermediate-risk (group 2, n = 52) was defined as recurrent grade 1 or newly diagnosed grade 2 tumor after GTR and treated with radiotherapy (54 Gy). High-risk (group 3, n = 53) included a newly diagnosed grade 2 tumor after STR, newly diagnosed grade 3 tumor, or recurrent grade 2 or 3 tumor and treated with radiotherapy (60 Gy). Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. The median follow-up times for the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk cohorts were 12.1, 12.0, and 11.1 years, respectively. The 10-year PFS and OS rates for the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk cohorts were 85.2% and 94.1%, 72.2% and 84.7%, and 42.5% and 51.1%, respectively. Five patients (9.6%) and eight patients (15.1%) had a grade 3+ toxicity attributed to radiotherapy in the intermediate- and high-risk cohorts, respectively. The long-term outcomes using this risk-adapted approach support observation for low-risk patients, inform radiotherapy patient selection and practice standards for intermediate- and high-risk patients, and provide comparative benchmarks for future trials.

papers.title: Improved Progression-Free Survival Following Dose-Escalated Versus Standard-Dose Postoperative Radiation Therapy for High-Risk Meningiomas: An International Multicenter Individual Patient–Level Meta-Analysis (FIRESTORM)
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: We performed an individual patient-level meta-analysis of high-risk meningiomas to compare the outcomes of dose-escalated radiation therapy (DE-RT) versus standard-dose postoperative radiation therapy (SD-RT).

METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 7 institutions participated. DE-RT was defined as treatment with a biologically effective dose of ≥79.2 Gy (equivalent of 66 Gy in 33 fractions). We compared progression-free survival (PFS) with DE-RT versus SD-RT via Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank t tests, a Cox proportional hazards multivariable model, and propensity score analyses with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). We also compared incidences of central nervous system radionecrosis (RN) with DE-RT versus SD-RT.

RESULTS: The analysis included 248 patients with high-risk meningioma (59 received DE-RT and 189 received SD-RT). One hundred and eighty-eight cases (75.8%) were World Health Organization grade 2, and 103 cases (41.5%) were recurrent meningiomas. Extent of resection was subtotal resection in 182 of 248 (75.2%). Three- and 5-year PFS rates were 62.8% (95% CI, 55.8%-69.0%) and 45.0% (95% CI, 37.3%-52.3%), respectively. DE-RT was associated with superior PFS rates (P = .0022), with 3-year (86.4% vs 55.6%) and 5-year (65.8% vs 38.8%) PFS rates favoring DE-RT. On multivariable analysis, DE-RT was associated with superior PFS (hazard ratio, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.24-0.69; P = .001). On IPTW, DE-RT continued to be associated with superior PFS (hazard ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.24-0.83; P = .01). A greater incidence of any grade RN was observed following DE-RT (20 of 59; 33.9%) versus SD-RT (25 of 189; 13.2%) (P = .001) but with similar grade 3 or greater RN events (DE-RT 5.1% vs SD-RT 3.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: DE-RT resulted in superior PFS for patients with high-risk meningiomas over SD-RT without an increase in severe toxicities.
